arguments.content: The ChatGPT relay loop split Gap 5 into two separate gaps that Anthony adopted. Gap 5A is active-metabolite efficacy misattribution: clinical effects assigned to parent CBD may partly track 7-OH-CBD, which the Epidiolex/DailyMed label identifies as active in preclinical seizure models and present at meaningful exposure. Gap 5B is high-AUC metabolite disposition/toxicity blindspot: 7-COOH-CBD is not seizure-active per the label, but has ~40-fold higher AUC than parent CBD after repeat oral dosing and has transporter consequences (P-gp substrate; BCRP/BSEP inhibition at clinically relevant concentrations). The corrected framing is that 7-COOH-CBD should not be called generally active without specifying axis, but it is pharmacologically consequential at the transporter/disposition layer. Anthony recognized this as Gap-2-in-reverse: parent-CBD targets may be out of reach at clinical free concentrations, while a metabolite nobody was measuring sits at much higher exposure and may drive liver/DDI signals. Future instances should keep 5A and 5B separate because split, each is surgically falsifiable.
